unit.why: A teaching against disparaging other tzaddikim, attributed to R. Hayyim of Sanz, built around one anecdote: R. David Zlates visits R. Meir of Premishlan, who takes offence at his praise of the Belzer, and David answers with a parable of tractates.
unit.boundary_note: the teaching's theme continues into the next division (quotation from סידור לב שמח)

stories.start_quote: ושמעתי כי פ״א בא הה״צ ר׳ דוד זלאטעס
stories.summary_en: R. David Zlates visits R. Meir of Premishlan and says he learned good-heartedness from the Belzer; R. Meir is offended, and R. David answers that each tzaddik is a separate tractate, which leads into a homily that hasidim may visit other tzaddikim and must not mock them.

tags.why: the short anecdote sits inside an extended homiletic and ethical frame

quotes: אם א׳ מחסידיו נוסע אל צדיק א׳
ואצל צדיק א׳ נוסע ללמוד ממנו איזה מדה
tags.why: the central subject is going to tzaddikim other than one's own rebbe

quotes: בא הה״צ ר׳ דוד זלאטעס לקבל פני אור עולם רבינו מאיר מפרימישלאן
tags.why: R. David comes to visit R. Meir

quotes: הסתכלות בפני הצדיק תועלה גדול לנשמה
tags.why: teaches binding oneself to tzaddikim, the benefit of gazing at a tzaddik's face, and faith in tzaddikim
R. Meir's offence at praise of a rival tzaddik

quotes: ואלו היה שלום בין הצדיקים והחסידים
tags.why: relations among tzaddikim and between hasidim of different courts
good-heartedness is the virtue learned from the Belzer

tags.why: exegesis of a verse given as the tzaddik's teaching
